newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- RANK CARRIES ON DISPOSALS WITH SALE OF FILM LIBRARY

The Rank Group will today announce the 65 million pound stg sale of its film distribution company to Carlton Communications. Carlton is moving more into film and television following its digital broadcasting alliance with Granada and BSkyB, while Rank is continuing to concentrate more on other leisure and entertainment activities.
-- ORANGE READY FOR FRAUDSTERS AFTER TIP-OFF FROM VODAFONE

Orange is believed to be the latest intended target for a professional mobile telephone fraud operation. The group has been alerted by extensive advertising of cheap Orange phones in trade magazines. Vodafone, one of the early victims of the operation, is believed to have passed Orange a confidential list of names of those it believes responsible. Orange downplayed the threat, saying it believed it had systems well in control.
-- HOUSE PRICE RISE 'NOT A SIGNAL FOR RETURN TO BOOM'

Halifax Building Society figures released yesterday showed a rise in house prices of more than 7 percent in the first quarter. However, the society said the rise did not indicate a return to a 1980s-style boom, as prices were still 4.2 percent below their May 1989 peak.
THE TIMES
-- JAPAN BOLSTERS BANKS AFTER COLLAPSE

Japan's finance ministry was last night coping with the collapse of an affiliate of the Nippon Credit Bank, Japan's largest single corporate failure. Crown Leasing applied to be wound up with debts of about 1,060 billion yen, while Nippon Credit announced measures including a total pullout from overseas operations in an attempt to restore confidence.
-- ENGINEERING JOBS WARNING AS STRONG POUND HITS EXPORTS

The engineering industry, hit hard by the strength of sterling, is considering cutting jobs in order to stay competitive. Exports have fallen in the first quarter to -2 percent in March, compared with +9 percent in December, and it is feared imports will hit the industry further.
-- AMSTRAD IN VALUE PLEDGE TO INVESTORS

Amstrad yesterday sold Dancall, its Danish mobile-phone subsidiary, to Robert Bosch of Germany for 92 million pounds stg. The company is expected to return value to shareholders via a special dividend, a share buyback or possibly a demerger of remaining operations. Shares rose 2.5p to 221.5p.
THE GUARDIAN
-- U.S. RATE FEAR RATTLES MARKETS

International stock markets fell sharply yesterday in response to fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve may raise American interest rates soon. The Dow Jones industrial average fell as much as 60 points on early trading, following earlier falls in Europe and Asia in response to the previous American falls.
-- 20 MILLION POUND HOTEL FRAUDSTER JAILED

Former hotels entrepreneur Robert Feld was yesterday sentenced to jail for eight years after being convicted of a 20 million pound stg fraud. All counts related to the 20 million pound rights issue of new shares in Resort Hotels offered in 1992. Victims included about 5,000 small shareholders.
-- JOBS BREWING AT PUB CHAIN

JD Wetherspoon pubs have announced plans to create 10,000 jobs over five years by opening 350 new pubs nationwide. 5,500 of the new jobs will be part-time. The group dismissed rumours that a bid was being prepared by rivals Scottish & Newcastle.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- MARKS & SPENCER TRIES ON CLOTHES BY MAIL ORDER

Marks & Spencer is to expand its home shopping operation next year, with the introduction of clothing catalogues. The move is part of a growing swing towards providing home shopping services by U.K. retailers in response to consumer interest. The Marks move follows successful operations with home furnishings, flowers, hampers and wine.
-- INSTITUTIONS WORRY OVER BT MERGER

British Telecom is facing institutional shareholder resistance over its proposed merger with MCI, its U.S. partner, only two weeks before the deal is due to be voted on. Large institutions are understood to have requested further meetings to clarify BT's stand. MCI shareholders in the U.S. are due to vote today.
-- LABOUR BACKS TASKFORCE 2000

Labour has pledged to continue funding Taskforce 2000, the government-sponsored body created to publicise the millennium computer timebomb. The Department of Trade and Industry is believed to have offered short-term funds to help the body through its cash troubles.
